title: Memtara Canonical Case File pack, v1
description: The structure of decision_evidence.json inside an offline verification bundle. This is the projection `build_pack()` in scripts/export_audit_evidence.py copies out of the wealth-assessment evidence endpoint, serialised canonically (sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace) and hashed into the seal's canonical_evidence_sha256. NOTE ON SCOPE: this is the *pack* schema that exists today, not the DecisionEvidence v1 schema specified in the board response. It has no model.*, no human_review.*, no consent.* and no policy_version, because the system does not record them. A schema that declared those fields would describe a record this codebase cannot produce.
x_every_key_is_required: Deliberate. A rejected assessment must produce the same shape as an approved one: `suitable` is a tri-state value (true/false/null), never an absent key. Optional fields that vanish on a decline would change the canonical byte layout, which is itself a detectable defect.

terms_assessed_against.description: The firm's thresholds, snapshotted when the assessment was opened. These are public inputs 4-7 and they are the firm's, not the client's.

outcome.description: The decision. `suitable` is read from public input 11, the circuit's return value. It is NOT the exit code of `bb verify`.

suitable.description: true = suitable, false = not suitable, null = never assessed. Three distinct facts; null must never be read as a decline.

sha256.description: SHA-256 over the vk file's bytes, as computed by the server that used it. This is NOT the value in circuits/wealth_suitability/vkey/vk_hash, which is Barretenberg's own field-element commitment to the key.

proofs.description: Every submission, accepted and rejected alike.

proof_bytes.description: The LENGTH of the proof in bytes, not the proof. The evidence endpoint returns a count (wealth/evidence.rs: `p.proof_bytes.len()`); the proof itself must be supplied separately and is checked against proof_sha256.

public_inputs.description: 12 field elements as 0x-prefixed hex, in circuit order. Index 11 is the verdict.

audit_chain_excerpt.description: This request's own events from Memtara's global hash chain. `seq` values are not expected to be consecutive: the chain is global across tenants, so other assessments were interleaved.

proof_token.description: The Memtara-issued JWT, if the firm kept it. The server does not retain it.
